summary: French Valley sits in the broad, sun-drenched inland plateau between the Santa Rosa Plateau to the west and the low granite hills east of Temecula, and that geography hands it something unusual for a community of 42,500: nearly unbroken sightlines toward ridgelines that catch golden-hour light roughly 300 evenings a year, thanks to an average of ten hours of daily sunshine and highs that hover near 77°F. Despite the open-sky setting, this is fundamentally a bedroom community; the nearest major employment clusters — logistics hubs along the I-15 corridor, healthcare systems in Murrieta and Temecula, and a scattering of defense-adjacent firms near March Air Reserve Base — all require a car commute, and many residents drive north toward Riverside or even into San Diego County. The home-price-to-income ratio lands around 4.8×, and median rent at $3,016 consumes roughly 27% of the median household's gross income — tight but serviceable compared to coastal Southern California. The street network is largely master-planned subdivisions connected by wide arterials rather than a walkable grid, and there is no real downtown core with sit-down restaurants or evening foot traffic; retail gravitates toward nearby Temecula's commercial strips.
